lastText: File ClosedThe Seam in the WallMinor VictorySoviet High Command, 1941–1945End of hostilities: JUNE 1945 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives close to the historical schedule, around June 1945. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over: a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The tank armies waited for the three fronts to close together and entered Prague on May 11, two days later than they did in the real war. The Izyum salient was given up before the Germans could close it. The armies, tanks and guns the real offensive lost in May 1942 went into the summer instead, and Case Blue met a southern front that had them. The autumn 1942 reserve was weighted entirely south: Mars never launched, the Rzhev grinder's cost declined, and the single-theater concentration tested against the pinning argument Mars's defenders always made. Germany's defeat was not a variable Soviet command decisions controlled, only its timing and its price.One Year LaterVictory arrived close to the historical May 8, 1945, and the year that follows tracks the historical one closely: the Red Army's occupation zone, the machinery of a new political order installed behind it, and a wartime alliance already audibly disagreeing about what Europe's map is supposed to mean now that the shooting has stopped.
